title: Middle and Passive Voice
objectives: Recognize middle voice meanings (reflexive, intensive, etc.)
Form present middle/passive for all conjugations

grammar.explanation: In the present, imperfect, and perfect, Greek uses the same forms for middle and passive. Context determines which is meant. The middle expresses action done to or for oneself; the passive expresses receiving action.
rules: Deponent verbs: middle/passive form, active meaning
Aorist has distinct forms for middle (-σάμην) and passive (-θην)
Future middle/passive also distinguished in form

exercises.question: Middle or passive? ὁ παῖς λούεται.
Translate: ὁ λόγος ἐλέχθη ὑπὸ τοῦ προφήτου.
exercises.answer: The word was spoken by the prophet.

readingPassage.greek: Οἱ μαθηταὶ ἀπεκρίναντο τῷ διδασκάλῳ. Βουλόμεθα τὴν ἀλήθειαν μαθεῖν. Οὐ δυνάμεθα τοῦτο ποιεῖν. Ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ κηρύσσεται ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ.
readingPassage.translation: The disciples answered the teacher. We wish to learn the truth. We are not able to do this. The word of God is being preached in all the earth.
